fragments.text: This speech is on the importance of media law in the field of AI and information access. When we talk about how artificial intelligence is changing the way we access information, the media law plays the central role. Media such as the press and broadcasters provide us with information we need to make informed decision, for example, in elections or emergencies, but also in everyday life. But the media landscape is facing major challenges today. Traditional media companies are facing a significant reduction in their reach and presence across Europe, particularly in rural areas. At the same time, the digital transformation has radically changed the way information is produced, distributed and consumed. New dependencies on large technology companies or algorithm driven platforms are also emerging.
fragments.summary: This speech is on the importance of media law in the field of AI and information access.

fragments.text: One of the biggest dangers is the increasing dependence on large AI providers and technology companies. These companies control the algorithms and technologies used in media companies. This allows them to dictate their terms and influence the way information is disseminated. This concentration of power with a few providers carries the risk that media companies had less control over their own content and work processes and become dependent on the business models and decisions of AI providers. Another risk lies in the possibility of blurring the line between human journalism and AI generated content. If readers and viewers can no longer distinguish whether an article or contribution was created by a human or an AI, there is a risk of loss of trust in the media.
fragments.summary: One of the biggest dangers is the increasing dependence on large AI providers and technology companies.

fragments.text: The authenticity and credibility of news could suffer as a result which could lead to increasing uncertainty and skepticism towards media content. AI is playing an increasingly important role in the distribution of content, especially on social media. Algorithms decide which content is shown, the users and which is not. This carries the risk that AI often opaque and without human oversight influences public opinion. Algorithms often prioritize content based on high engagement rates, which can lead to an increased distribution of sensational news or polarizing content. An opinionated AI could thus jeopardize the media balance and diversity of opinions by deciding what information is visible to users. These risks show that the use of AI in the media should not take place without precautionary measures.

fragments.text: It is important to develop ethical standards and create legal frameworks to ensure that AI is used responsibility responsibly and in accordance with the principles of journalism. Only in this way can the opportunities offered by AI be fully exploited without jeopardizing the integrity and diversity of the media landscape and the right to access information. The law plays a crucial role in balancing the opportunities and risks of AI in the media landscape. It can create framework conditions that both promote the innovative power of AI and mitigate its potential risks. There are already initial legal regulations in Germany and Europe on one of the central issues, namely the starting point of transparency in the functioning of algorithms that decide on the distribution of content.
fragments.summary: It is important to develop ethical standards and create legal frameworks to ensure that AI is used responsibility responsibly and in accordance with the principles of journalism.

Overall, the law has a task of creating a balance that both harnesses the benefit of AI and minimise the associated risks. Transparency and non-discrimination are key principles that can help preserve the integrity and diversity of the media landscape and protect the public from unwanted influences from AI-powered technologies.
